- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak values by 2–5%.
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by high sentiment, forecast often overshoots; cap peak values at 1–2% above recent 7-day average.
- When sentiment dips below 0.33, model often fails to correct downward trend; adjust forecast downward by 1–3% relative to prior 3-day average.
- Model underestimates prices when sentiment is neutral or negative (≤0.33) and recent price is trending down; add 1–2% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- If model forecast is >10% above true outcome for 3+ consecutive days, apply mean reversion: subtract 1–3% per day until forecast aligns with 10-day moving average.
- For 30-day forecasts, if sentiment is high and price is trending upward, model often overfits; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% to avoid overextension.
- When sentiment is high but price is flat or slightly declining, model tends to overreact; reduce forecast by 1–2% to match sentiment’s cautionary tone.
- If true outcome shows sudden drop after model peak, apply “lag correction”: reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 3 days to reflect sentiment’s delayed reaction.
